title: Ramakrishna takes a teacher
hookLine: even Ramakrishna, lost in love for Kali, took a tantric teacher
carry: tantra is received from a guru, through diksha
tomorrow: the teacher whispers one syllable. what's inside it?

lines: A PRIEST LOST IN LOVE FOR KALI.
cards: In 1861 a wandering woman ascetic came to the Kali temple at Dakshineswar, near Calcutta. People called her the Bhairavi Brahmani, and she knew the Tantras deeply.
The temple's young priest, Ramakrishna, was already lost in love for the goddess Kali, so lost that some people thought him mad. She didn't.
She became his teacher, and over the next years guided him, step by step, through the tantric disciplines.

teach.h: DIKSHA: THE KEY IS A PERSON.
teach.b: Why would someone so devoted need a teacher? Because in the tantric way, the key isn't printed in the book. It's a person: the guru.
A practice begins with diksha, initiation, when the teacher gives the student a mantra and the right to use it.

The Kularnava Tantra praises the guru in the highest terms: the student is to see the teacher as Shiva himself, in a human form close enough to speak to. That's a lot to hand any human being, and the same book knows it.

teach.h: MANY TAKE WEALTH. FEW TAKE SUFFERING.
teach.b: Teachers who take a student's wealth are easy to find, it warns; a teacher who takes away a student's suffering is rare.
So it asks for care both ways: the teacher tests the student, and the student looks for a teacher who lives what they teach.
That's one more answer to what tantra actually is: not a technique lifted off a page, but something handed on, person to person.
It's also why Hindu families still honor teachers: on Guru Purnima, a full moon each summer, many bow to the people who taught them.
And look at what this week handed on. Lila's room, holding a world. Chudala, free at home.
The grip, not the things. A king who went home free. Rama, freed while living.
And a word with a reputation, opened like a book.

how: In tantric lineages a student is initiated by a guru, who gives a mantra in person; Ramakrishna's years with the Bhairavi Brahmani are a well-known example. Many Hindus honor their teachers on Guru Purnima, and greet teachers and elders with folded hands or by touching their feet.

games.q: what does “what tantra actually is” mean?
o: a practice handed on by a living teacher, through initiation
a secret code only scholars can crack from old books
a set of exercises anyone can learn from a page

games.q: the teacher and the student — tap the pairs.
p: the teacher, seen as Shiva in human form
the woman who taught Ramakrishna tantra

the Kularnava warns about teachers who take a student's wealth
easy to find, it says; one who takes away suffering is rare.

games.q: a friend wants to learn classical singing from videos alone. her grandmother says find a real teacher. by the Kularnava's logic, what's the grandmother's best case?
o: some things are handed on in person, not off a page.
videos are wrong about everything they teach.
teachers are only for people who can't read.
games.why: in the Kularnava, the key isn't printed in the book: practice begins when a living teacher hands it on, through diksha. hindu music is taught the same way, guru to student.

practice: In many Hindu homes, you greet a teacher or an elder with folded hands, or bend to touch their feet. Let's borrow that. Bring to mind one person who handed something on to you in person: a grandparent, a music teacher, a coach.

Fold your hands, bow your head a little toward them, and say out loud, quietly, one thing they taught you, in their words if you can. Then sit with it, and with them, for the rest of the time. If you pray, give thanks for them.
If you don't, the bow and the thank you are enough.

wordCard.voice: What tantra actually is: here, a practice received from a living teacher through diksha, as Ramakrishna received it, not lifted from a page.

orig.note: Sanskrit diksha: initiation, when a teacher gives a student a mantra.

carryVoice: Keep this one: tantra is received from a guru, through diksha. Handed on, person to person. A week, done.

sources.ref: Swami Saradananda, Sri Ramakrishna the Great Master (the Bhairavi Brahmani's arrival at Dakshineswar in 1861 and her guiding Ramakrishna through the tantric disciplines)
Kularnava Tantra, chapters on the guru and initiation (the guru as Shiva in human form; teachers who take the disciple's wealth are many, one who removes the disciple's suffering is rare)
Kularnava Tantra, on diksha and on examining teacher and student
Guru Purnima (Vyasa Purnima), the full moon of Ashadha, when many Hindus honor their teachers; pranam and touching the feet of teachers and elders as common Hindu gestures of respect
